### **1. Molality Calculation**
* **Given:**
  * Mass of solute ($H_2SO_4$) = $392 	ext{ g}$
  * Volume of water = $1 	ext{ L} ightarrow 	ext{Mass of solvent (water)} = 1000 	ext{ g} = 1 	ext{ kg}$ (assuming density of water = $1 	ext{ kg/L}$)
  * Molar mass of $H_2SO_4 = (2 \times 1) + 32 + (4 \times 16) = 98 	ext{ g/mol}$

* **Formula:**
  $$\text{Molality } (m) = \frac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Mass of solvent in kg}}$$

* **Calculation:**
  $$\text{Moles of } H_2SO_4 = \frac{392 \text{ g}}{98 \text{ g/mol}} = 4 \text{ moles}$$
  $$\text{Molality } (m) = \frac{4 \text{ moles}}{1 \text{ kg}} = 4 \text{ mol/kg (or 4 m)}$$

---

### **2. Definitions**
* **Normality ($N$):** The number of gram-equivalents of solute dissolved per liter of solution.
  $$N = \frac{\text{Gram equivalents}}{\text{Volume of solution in liters}}$$
* **Molarity ($M$):** The number of moles of solute dissolved per liter of solution.
  $$M = \frac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Volume of solution in liters}}$$
* **Molality ($m$):** The number of moles of solute dissolved per kilogram of solvent.
  $$m = \frac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Mass of solvent in kg}}$$
proTip: Note that molality uses mass of solvent in kg, whereas molarity uses volume of solution in liters.
